summary:
Little Rovers is a three-book series of early readers that introduces NASA hardware still on the Moon and Mars to the youngest space fans: children ages 4–5. In each book, a machine tells its own story in the first person. Book 1 follows the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (1971), Book 2 follows Sojourner, the first rover on Mars (1997), and Book 3 follows Opportunity (2004–2018). Each book ends by telling readers where the machine is today: “I am still on the Moon!” or “I am still on Mars!”

The books use one or two short sentences per page, repeated lines, the Andika typeface designed for beginning readers, and a text description for every picture. Counting and picture-word pages build early literacy, and a “For grown-ups” page in each book gives the real mission facts, NASA sources and questions to talk about.

Most information about past missions is written for adults. Little Rovers turns real NASA history into stories young children can read themselves, sparking curiosity about space science at the age when it starts.
details:
Little Rovers is a three-book series of early readers for children ages 4–5 about NASA hardware still on the Moon and Mars. In each book, the machine tells its own story. Book 1, Moon Buggy, is the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (1971). Book 2, Little Rover, Big Mars, is Sojourner, the first rover on Mars (1997). Book 3, Oppy’s Big Adventure, is Opportunity (2004–2018). Every story goes from launch (“Up, up, up! Zoom!”) to landing and discovery, and ends by telling the reader where the machine is today: “I am still on the Moon!” or “I am still on Mars!” Each book also has a counting page, a picture-word page and a “For grown-ups” page with real mission facts, NASA sources and questions to talk about.

Most information about past missions is written for adults. Little Rovers lets the youngest space fans read real NASA history by themselves. It builds early reading skills and sparks curiosity about space at the age when it starts. Parents and teachers get accurate facts to keep the conversation going.

We used Claude, an SI assistant, to draft the text and illustrations and to build the books and slide deck as web pages (HTML, CSS and SVG). Every SI-made illustration is labeled “SI-generated.” The text uses Andika, a free font designed for beginning readers. Every fact was checked against NASA sources, including NASA mission pages, the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive, NASA JPL and NASA Astrobiology.

The project is creative because the robots tell their own stories in words a preschooler can read. Lines repeat across all three books, so children learn the pattern and read along. Each ending links past missions to where the hardware is today.

Team Little Tigers is Ashneer, age 4.5 [Mom as his helper only if he asked for it]. Ashneer chose what rovers he wanted to book to be and vibe coded using the dictate option of Claude to tell what he wanted in the book. We focused on short sentences and repetition, large high-contrast letters, a description of every picture for screen readers, gentle endings for young children, facts checked against NASA, and honest labeling of SI-made content. He himself read all the 3 books and checked if anything was incorrect based on the story he heard about all the 3 rovers.
